recipe: When designing an enum for WebAssembly, ensure all members fit within the range of `int` so the enum is represented as `i32` rather than `i64`.
trigger_condition: Defining an enum type in C code targeting the WebAssembly Basic C ABI.
evidence: An `enum` is `i32` if all the members of the `enum` can be represented by an `int`.

recipe: Represent `__int128_t` and `__uint128_t` as a struct containing two `i64` fields in little-endian order, and pass them as two `i64` values in little-endian order.
trigger_condition: Working with 128-bit integer types in C code targeting WebAssembly.
evidence: `__int128_t` and `__uint128_t` are passed as two `i64`s in little-endian order, and are otherwise represented in the ABI as a struct containing two `i64` fields, in little-endian order.

recipe: When defining C structures or unions, account for the fact that the overall alignment is determined by the most strictly aligned component, and each member is placed at the lowest available offset with appropriate alignment.
trigger_condition: Designing struct or union layouts in C for WebAssembly.
evidence: Structures and unions assume the alignment of their most strictly aligned component.

recipe: Remember that local or global array variables of length at least 16 bytes, and C99 variable-length arrays, always receive an alignment of at least 16 bytes, which may affect your layout calculations.
trigger_condition: Declaring array variables in C code targeting WebAssembly.
evidence: a local or global array variable of length at least 16 bytes or a C99 variable-length array variable always has alignment of at least 16 bytes

recipe: When using bit-fields in C struct or union definitions, remember they are allocated from right to left and must be contained within a storage unit appropriate for their declared type.
trigger_condition: Using bit-fields in C struct or union definitions for WebAssembly.
evidence: bit-fields are allocated from right to left

recipe: Place address-taken local C variables on the linear stack in linear memory rather than in the wasm local value space, since the runtime call stack is not visible in linear memory.
trigger_condition: Taking the address of a local variable in C code targeting WebAssembly.
evidence: address-taken local C variables need to be on a separate stack in the linear memory

recipe: Maintain 16-byte alignment for the stack pointer global when managing stack frames in WebAssembly.
trigger_condition: Managing stack frame layout in WebAssembly function implementations.
evidence: The stack pointer global (`SP`) points to the bottom of the stack frame and always has 16-byte alignment.

recipe: For leaf functions that need less than 128 bytes of stack space, you may skip updating the stack pointer in the prolog and epilog by writing into the 128-byte red zone below the stack pointer.
trigger_condition: Writing leaf functions in WebAssembly that require less than 128 bytes of stack space.
evidence: So a leaf function which needs less than 128 bytes of stack space need not update the stack pointer in its prolog or epilog at all.

recipe: When passing struct or union data indirectly via pointer, make a copy of the data if the callee should not modify it, since the callee is allowed to modify the pointed-to memory.
trigger_condition: Passing non-scalar struct or union data indirectly in WebAssembly function calls.
evidence: The callee is allowed to modify the contents of that memory, so the caller is responsible for making a copy of any indirectly passed data that the callee should not modify.

recipe: For varargs functions, place all variable arguments in a buffer arranged in order at the lowest appropriately aligned address, and pass a pointer to that buffer as the last parameter.
trigger_condition: Implementing varargs functions in C code targeting WebAssembly.
evidence: Varargs are placed in a buffer by the caller and the last parameter to the function is a pointer to that buffer.

recipe: Sign-extend signed 8-bit and 16-bit scalar values and zero-extend unsigned 8-bit and 16-bit scalar values before passing them as function arguments or returning them from functions.
trigger_condition: Passing or returning small integer types as function arguments in WebAssembly.
evidence: Signed 8 and 16-bit scalars are sign-extended, and unsigned 8 and 16-bit scalars are zero-extended before passing or returning.

recipe: Write your C/C++ source using the standard `main` function name; the compiler handles the ABI symbol mapping for you.
trigger_condition: When writing C or C++ code that will be compiled to WebAssembly
evidence: C and C++ source should continue to use the standard `main` name, and compilers will handle the details of conforming to the ABI.

recipe: Do not use an `envp` parameter in your main function; use `getenv` instead to access environment variables.
trigger_condition: When writing the main entrypoint for a WebAssembly C program
evidence: the wasm C ABI doesn't support an `envp` parameter. Fortunately, `envp` is not required by C, POSIX, or any other relevant standards, and is generally considered obsolete in favor of `getenv`.

recipe: Be aware that global constructors may execute before your main function, so main is not necessarily the first code to run.
trigger_condition: When designing program flow or initialization order in a WebAssembly C program
evidence: this may not be the first function in the program to be called, as programs may also have global constructors which run before it.

recipe: Do not conflate C ABI symbol names with WebAssembly export names when working with module exports.
trigger_condition: When dealing with WebAssembly module export names or toolchain export behavior
evidence: C symbol names are distinct from WebAssembly export names, which are outside the scope of the C ABI.
